subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: For non-group, not-from-me iMessage DMs where sender canonicalizes to destination_caller_id, should OpenClaw only repair when a canonical peer is recoverable, or should it also drop fail-closed when no peer can be recovered before access control?
rationale: That choice controls whether ambiguous local-sender payloads can reach authorization, pairing, routing, and reply delivery, and it is a security-boundary policy decision rather than a purely mechanical refactor.

options.title: Repair Only Confident Canonical Peers
options.body: Require canonical normalizeIMessageHandle comparisons, repair only when a distinct peer is found, and require live after-fix proof before merge.

options.title: Add Fail-Closed Guard
options.body: Repair confident peers and drop ambiguous local-sender DMs before access control when the peer cannot be recovered safely.

options.title: Pause This Branch
options.body: If the author’s remaining failure is a different root cause, pause this branch and track the narrower iMessage identity issue separately.

recommendation.title: Repair Only Confident Canonical Peers
recommendation.body: Require canonical normalizeIMessageHandle comparisons, repair only when a distinct peer is found, and require live after-fix proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work by neeravmakwana established the destination_caller_id self-chat classification behavior this decision builds on.
